---
title: "Search"
---

The *Search* tab is open to those that are SSO logged in. If you are not
logged in, you will see a message asking you to log in before you can search.

The tab has three parts: a filter panel on the left, a search field with
results list in the centre, and a map on the right.

## Item view

Above the results list is a search field (*Search title or description*). Type
a query and press *Search* (or submit the form); the Fair Data Finder searches
registered items by title, description, and related metadata, and shows matching
datasets in the list. Active filters and the query appear as chips that you can
clear individually, or all at once with *Clear filters*.

On the left, the *Filter* panel lets you narrow results by:

- *Domain* — one or more expertise domains
- *Keyword* — one or more keywords
- *Start date* / *End date* — temporal range of the dataset
- *Area* — set by drawing a polygon on the map (see [Map](#map))

Each result card shows the title, a short description, domain, optional
thumbnail, date information, and a link to the first asset when available.
Datasets without geometry are marked as *Global Dataset*. From a card you can:

- click *View details* to open the full item page (description, geometry map if
  present, assets, properties, and providers)
- click *Zoom to data* (when the item has a bounding box) to focus that item on
  the map

## Map

The right-hand side shows the current search results on a map. Datasets with
geometry appear as clustered point markers and/or footprints (polygons or
lines). Global datasets without geometry are not drawn on the map.

To restrict the search to a geographic area, use the polygon draw tool on the
map (top-left). Drawing a polygon filters results to items that intersect that
area; an *Area: Selected* chip appears with the other filters. Use the trash
control to clear the drawn area and remove the area filter.

Clicking a marker or footprint selects that item, zooms to it, and opens a
popup with title, description, asset link, and *View details*. Clicking empty
map space clears the selection. The map automatically fits to the extent of the
current results when no area filter is active.
